paragraphs: In Newcastle upon Tyne, children in care live with carers approved by Newcastle City Council's fostering service or by independent agencies such as those listed below. The council is one of twelve North East councils in Foster with North East, the regional hub led from Sunderland, so enquiries from within 50 miles of the city go through the hub first.

Newcastle offers an unusually wide range of fostering: respite, short-term and long-term care, emergency care with a retainer, parent and child, short breaks for disabled children, supported lodgings for 16 to 21 year olds, and a pilot for children seeking sanctuary. Two schemes, Build a Future and Change a Future, are for young people in or close to residential care and ask for professional experience of working with young people who are hard to reach. Carers can be approved for more than one kind.

The council's process runs from enquiry and a home visit to an invitation to apply, then an assessment of four to six months with medical and DBS checks, references and the Skills to Foster course, then panel and approval. Support includes a supervising social worker, a 24-hour phone line, therapeutic staff, training and a Mockingbird-style carer community.

Newcastle pays a weekly allowance for each child by age plus a fee that rises with the child's needs; our Newcastle allowance page shows that a Tier 1 carer receives £288.65 to £426.98 a week for one child. Compare that with what two or three of the agencies below offer before you decide.
